clue.text: One philosopher said to be a spin bowler …

indicators.note: said signals that the philosopher's name is heard rather than read, giving a word sounding the same

parts.note: John Locke was the English empiricist philosopher

explanation.surface: A puzzling claim that a thinker was really a slow bowler at cricket, with the ellipsis running on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Lock was an England left-arm spin bowler of the 1950s; cricket is the British bat-and-ball game. The ellipsis ties this clue to 3-across, where a second philosopher sounds like another cricketer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Lock was a famous England spinner, so his surname names a spin bowler.

clue.text: Sticklers among the top people surrounded by members

indicators.note: surrounded by shows the top people sit inside the members

parts.note: legs are limbs, or members of the body
the A-list is the set of top celebrities

explanation.surface: Pedantic types among the elite, hemmed in by club members.
explanation.definitionFit: People who insist on the letter of the law are sticklers for rules.

clue.text: Fixed continent, as some might say, for certain mammals

indicators.note: a pronunciation some speakers might use, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: fixed is set and the continent is Asia

explanation.surface: An oddly worded remark about a settled landmass and some animals.
explanation.definitionFit: The order of whales, dolphins and porpoises is a group of marine mammals.

clue.text: … and his contemporary said to be an opening batsman

indicators.note: said signals that the contemporary's name is heard rather than read, giving a word sounding the same

parts.note: Thomas Hobbes was a seventeenth-century English philosopher, a contemporary of John Locke from the previous clue

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: another thinker of the same era is said to have opened the batting.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Hobbs was a great England opening batsman in cricket, the British bat-and-ball game. 'His' refers back to Locke in 1-across, and the leading ellipsis signals the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Hobbs opened the innings for Surrey and England, so his surname names an opening batsman.

clue.text: A rest home dished out what most of us wouldn't want to eat

definitions.text: what most of us wouldn't want to eat

indicators.note: dished out suggests the letters are served up in a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A care home served something residents wouldn't fancy on their plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Flesh from a horse is a food most British people refuse, so it is a fair description.

clue.text: Animal making part of circular path in regular journey

indicators.note: in places the curved segment inside the regular route

parts.note: a beat is the regular round of a police officer
an arc is part of a circle

explanation.surface: A creature runs part of a circuit during its usual round.
explanation.definitionFit: The binturong of Asia, or the red panda, is called by this name, so it is an animal.

clue.text: Ultimately this bird disappeared crossing a group of islands

indicators.note: crossing means stretching across, so the outer pieces span the letter a
ultimately picks the final letter of this

parts.note: the moa is an extinct flightless bird of New Zealand

explanation.surface: A bird finally vanished while flying over a group of islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disappeared' is not a deletion signal; it describes the moa as extinct.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific nation is an archipelago, a cluster of islands.

clue.text: Prepared envelope, inside being strong and secure

indicators.note: inside places the letter for strong within the envelope abbreviation

parts.note: SAE is a stamped addressed envelope, one prepared in advance for a reply
F stands for forte, the musical direction meaning loud or strong

explanation.surface: An envelope made ready, with something strong inside it, is kept secure.
explanation.walkthrough: SAE (stamped addressed envelope) is a British abbreviation for the envelope you enclose for a reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something protected from danger or loss.

clue.text: Prison car crashed — something for recycling merchant

indicators.note: crashed suggests the letters are smashed up and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A prison van is wrecked and ends up at the scrapyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste metal sold for melting down is what a scrap dealer handles.

clue.text: Expression of disgust about Scottish tourist trap? Tact is needed

indicators.note: about means going around, so the expression of disgust surrounds the Scottish loch

parts.note: fie is an old exclamation of disgust
Loch Ness in Scotland draws tourists hoping to see its monster

explanation.surface: Diplomacy is needed when complaining about a Scottish tourist spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Loch Ness is the Scottish lake famed for its supposed monster.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicate skill in handling people is a synonym for tact.

clue.text: Man muttered, drunk with grog — a victory for evil

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters stagger about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man mumbles after too much grog, a sorry outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Wagner's opera means the twilight of the gods, the downfall of the old order to destructive forces.

clue.text: The fellow beset by insects in tree

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the insects enclose the fellow

parts.note: lice are small parasitic insects
HE is the pronoun for the fellow

explanation.surface: A man up a tree is plagued by insects.
explanation.definitionFit: The lychee, also spelt this way, is a Chinese fruit tree.

clue.text: Female game requiring inner application

indicators.note: requiring an inner part means the game must have the next piece placed inside it

parts.note: chess is the board game
an app is short for an application on a phone or computer

explanation.surface: A woman plays a game that demands inward commitment.
explanation.definitionFit: A jocular feminine form of chap, meaning a woman.

clue.text: Box of salt

parts.note: a salt is an old sailor, so his box is the trunk a seaman keeps his belongings in, not a salt cellar

explanation.surface: Seems to be a container of table salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' is the slang for a seasoned sailor ('old salt'), so the box belongs to him.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor's storage trunk is the box an old salt owns.

clue.text: Shared accommodation as custom in one sort of school

definitions.note: a verb phrase: lived together, sharing a home

indicators.note: in places the custom inside the school type

parts.note: a coed school is one for both boys and girls
a habit is a custom

explanation.surface: Pupils lived together as was customary at a certain kind of school.
explanation.definitionFit: To live together as a couple is to share a home.

clue.text: Bit TV cop has left behind

indicators.note: behind places the letter for left after the detective's name

parts.note: Inspector Morse is the Oxford detective of British television

explanation.surface: A television detective has departed, leaving only a scrap behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse is the British TV detective series set in Oxford. 'left behind' reads as one phrase but splits: L, with 'behind' putting it at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A small piece or scrap, especially of food, is a bit.

clue.text: Like part of body that's source of energy, sluggish in girl

indicators.note: in places the energy and sluggishness inside the girl's name

parts.note: Mary is a girl's name

indicators.note: source of picks the opening letter of energy, where the word begins

parts.note: dull means sluggish

explanation.surface: A girl has a body part that drains her energy and leaves her sluggish.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to marrow or the medulla, an inner part of a body organ.

clue.text: Behold, two positive responses in northern half of capital!

indicators.note: in places the two answers inside the truncated capital
in a down clue the northern half is the top half, so the capital loses its last three letters

parts.note: London is the UK capital
aye and yes both mean yes

explanation.surface: An exclamation of wonder at hearing two yeses in north London.
explanation.definitionFit: To set eyes on something is to see it, the meaning of behold.

clue.text: Greedy female with endless animosity, I couldn't care less

parts.note: a sow is a female pig, proverbially greedy

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word for animosity is cut

parts.note: hate is strong animosity

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a grasping, spiteful woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom expressing indifference, the same dismissive attitude.

clue.text: Speech from Horatio Nelson

indicators.note: from shows the letters are taken out of the admiral's name

explanation.surface: A speech by Admiral Nelson, perhaps before Trafalgar.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal public address is a speech.

clue.text: Criticise essay in which journalist's shown dogmatism

indicators.note: in which shows the journalist is placed within the words formed by criticise and essay

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly
ED, an editor, is the usual crossword journalist
to essay is to try

explanation.surface: A critic attacks an essay in which a journalist has shown a dogmatic attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive fussiness over rules and detail is a close relation of rigid insistence, so the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: Persons in trouble keep going

indicators.note: in trouble suggests the letters are in disorder

explanation.surface: People in difficulty carry on regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: To continue in spite of difficulty is to persevere, carry on.

clue.text: Reveal with insouciance solicitor full of rubbish

indicators.note: full of means the solicitor contains the rubbish

parts.note: a tout solicits custom, a solicitor in the literal sense
rot is rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: A careless lawyer speaking nonsense lets something slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' looks like a British lawyer but means anyone soliciting business: a tout.
explanation.definitionFit: To produce something casually, like a stock excuse, is to bring it out without care.

clue.text: Party crush — put up with being at back of queue

parts.note: a jam is a crush of people or traffic
to bear is to put up with, and its past tense gives this word

indicators.note: at back of picks the final letter of queue

explanation.surface: A crowded party where you have to tolerate standing at the end of the queue.
explanation.definitionFit: A large celebration or gathering, especially a scout rally, is a big party.

clue.text: Fish needs tap to get black off its head

indicators.note: off its head means the first letter, here the one for black, is removed

parts.note: to broach a cask is to tap it
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A fish needs a tap to get dirt off its head.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: It's the French bread, not English, that's sour

parts.note: le is the French masculine article for the

indicators.note: not means the letter for English is removed from the word for bread

parts.note: bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: French bread, unlike the English kind, tastes tart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' looks like a loaf but is slang for cash.

clue.text: Son is smart with Latin possibly — so he'll avoid these?

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters might be arranged some other way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy good at Latin will steer clear of errors in his translations.
explanation.definitionFit: Errors in rendering one language into another are what a good classicist would avoid.

clue.text: Girl with goal to ensnare one

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

clue.text: Longing to go back to house and sweetheart

parts.note: a yen is a longing

explanation.surface: Homesickness for house and lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A term of endearment for a loved one, just like darling.

clue.text: Floor performance that's showy falls short

parts.note: a stunt is a showy performance or feat
